summary: Johannes Schneider is a scholar of Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies who earned his Magister at the University of Marburg. He held posts at FU Berlin, the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities, and the University of Munich.

Johannes Schubert worked in Tibetology and Sinology, studying at the University of Leipzig under Conrady, Francke, Franke, Schmitt, and Weller. He held posts at Leipzig University Library, Ahnenerbe, and the University of Leipzig, including a chair in Tibetology.

John A. Ardussi works in Tibetology and history/archaeology, having studied under MA supervisor Turrell V. Wylie and earned a PhD from Australian National University. His career includes posts at ELDEC Corporation and the CNRS.

John Alexander Jorgensen specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology. He earned an MA under Kenneth H. J. Gardiner at Australian National University, where he later held academic posts, and served as a Senior Lecturer at Griffith University.

John Alexander Stewart, a scholar of linguistics, studied at the University of Aberdeen. Following service in the Indian Civil Service (1905–1933), he served as Reader in Burmese at the University of London and held a post at SOAS.

John Allan was an Indologist and historian who studied at the universities of Edinburgh and Leipzig. He was Keeper of Coins and Medals at the British Museum and taught Sanskrit at University College London, SOAS, and Edinburgh.

John Avery was a scholar in Indology and linguistics who studied at Amherst College, the universities of Tübingen and Berlin, and under William Dwight Whitney. He later served as Professor of Greek at Grinnell College and Bowdoin College.

John B. Carman is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He held posts at Harvard University (~1963–2002) as Director and served as director of the Center for the Study of World Religions (~1973–1989).

John B. Cobb Jr. is a scholar of philosophy and religious studies who earned his PhD at the University of Chicago. He held professorships at Claremont School of Theology and Claremont Graduate University and co-founded the Center for Process Studies.

John Borthwick Gilchrist was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Edinburgh. He served in the East India Company, became principal of Fort William College, and was University College London's first Professor of Hindustani.
John Bray is a scholar in Tibetology and history/archaeology who studied under Tsering Dhundup Gonkatsang. He has held a post at the International Association for Ladakh Studies.
John Brockington is an Indologist who served at the University of Edinburgh, where he was attested as Senior Lecturer in Sanskrit in 1987 and as Professor of Sanskrit from 1998 to 2003.

John Brough, an Indologist and linguist, studied at Edinburgh and Cambridge under Arthur Berriedale Keith and Harold Walter Bailey. He held posts at the British Museum, SOAS, and served as Professor of Sanskrit at London and Cambridge.
John Buescher is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his doctoral dissertation at the University of Virginia in 1982 and served as Director at Voice of America.
John Burnet was a scholar of philosophy who studied at the University of Edinburgh and Balliol College, Oxford. He served on the faculty at the University of St Andrews from ~1892 to 1926.

John Burton-Page was an Indologist and historian who studied at the Royal College of Music and Oxford. He held academic posts at SOAS University of London and the Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute.
John C. Huntington was a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He served as a professor at Ohio State University, with his tenure attested between 1987 and 2000.

John C. Maraldo is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He spent his academic career at the University of North Florida, where he eventually became distinguished professor emeritus of philosophy.
John Caspar Leyden was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Edinburgh from ~1790 to 1797. In 1808, he served as professor of Hindustani at Fort William College.

John Chadwick was a linguist and classical historian educated at Corpus Christi College, Cambridge. He worked on the Oxford Latin Dictionary and served as Perceval Maitland Laurence Reader in Classics at the University of Cambridge.
